146488.title: The Forest in Winter at Sunset
146488.creator: Théodore Rousseau

source.institution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access

editorial.note: The Met dates it ca. 1846–67: Rousseau kept returning to the canvas for roughly two decades.
The Barbizon artists’ colony was located on the edge of the forest of Fontainebleau, southeast of Paris. Barbizon painters exerted a major influence on the Hague School.

This garden is somewhat enigmatic: where are we? The space is enclosed, you can barely see the sky. There are no people. There is no realistic light, nor any realistic representation of trees, grass, flowers.
